headline: Medium pairwise risk: shared allowlisted egress and browser/API surfaces create leakage and workflow-conflict pathways, but no direct shared-channel evidence is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP channel is documented between nuwa-skill and PaddleOCR, so direct prompt injection is not evidenced. The only plausible bridge is manual transfer of outputs into PaddleOCR’s document-processing flow, which is an unusual configuration and lower blast radius than default shared-channel cases.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies nuwa-skill output into PaddleOCR prompts or document text, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared workspace or message queue is added later, the pathway strengthens.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not paste raw model output into PaddleOCR inputs.
Add a human review step before any downstream use.
Use explicit delimiters for any copied text.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: nuwa-skill has allowlisted network egress and PaddleOCR processes documents and images with API calls, so sensitive document content could flow from one agent into the other’s outputs in default workflows. No shared workspace is documented, but the pair still presents a plausible leakage path through document ingestion and outbound requests.
conditions: IF sensitive documents are passed from nuwa-skill into PaddleOCR, those contents may be exposed in downstream outputs.
IF either agent is configured to upload full file contents to a third-party backend, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Restrict both agents to non-sensitive test data.
Disable outbound access except to approved endpoints.
Redact documents before OCR processing.
Review logs for accidental content capture.
requires-engineering: enforce per-file data-loss controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have allowlisted network egress, but neither profile shows unrestricted filesystem write, git mutation, or overlapping mutable OAuth scopes. The main conflict is limited to concurrent outbound requests or API usage, which is narrower than the rubric’s medium/high write-conflict cases.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same external API quota or rate-limited endpoint, contention can occur.
IF a shared mutable resource is added later, conflict severity increases.
mitigations: Stagger network-heavy jobs.
Set per-agent rate limits.
Use separate API keys where possible.
Monitor for 429 or quota errors.
requires-engineering: add locking for shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: PaddleOCR is a document-processing agent that can turn inputs into extracted text, and nuwa-skill is a research agent that may feed outputs onward; if one agent’s output is treated as authoritative by the other, errors can cascade. There is no direct evidence of verification steps, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF PaddleOCR output is consumed without verification by nuwa-skill, extraction errors can propagate.
IF nuwa-skill’s generated claims are rendered or acted on downstream, false facts can cascade.
mitigations: Require human review of extracted text.
Compare OCR output against source documents.
Flag low-confidence fields for manual checking.
Keep provenance metadata attached to outputs.
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or PHI-handling mismatch is documented for either nuwa-skill or PaddleOCR, and both are open-source with docs-only evidence. Because the profiles do not show regulated data classes or conflicting compliance regimes, only a low residual compliance concern remains.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is introduced into the workflow, compliance review is required.
IF deployment regions differ from data residency requirements, the risk increases.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in this pair.
Document the data flow and retention policy.
Confirm deployment region before use.
Review vendor terms for each endpoint.
requires-engineering: implement residency-aware routing.
